patch.signpost: A proof that statistically stationary solutions of 3D Navier-Stokes on the torus with white-in-time forcing have kinetic energy o(1/nu), which gives the averaged 4/5 law; or the zeroth law for a fixed smooth deterministic forcing; or a lab release with a turbulence-theory family.
patch.why: This is the theory engineering actually wants, because closures need statistics, not trajectories. It is harder than NS regularity in two respects: the right statements must be invented, so posing is part of the problem (judgment: 2-4 doublings plus posing), and only one answer counts, since the zeroth law for natural forcing may be false or unprovable in a given framework. At S2's 6-9 months per doubling, capability arrives late 2027 to late 2029; with posing and checking, 2030. S3 keeps Medium for the same truth risk, though it arrives a year earlier. One route carries little truth risk. With white-in-time forcing the noise fixes the mean energy input, and Bedrossian, Coti Zelati, Punshon-Smith and Weber (arXiv 1803.09695) proved the averaged 4/5 law for stationary martingale solutions on the torus assuming only that kinetic energy is o(1/nu). Simulations and experiment support that estimate, though it may need tools close to regularity theory. Chain: zeroth law and scaling, then a rigorous LES convergence theory (prop-les-convergence-theory, now merged into frontier-certified-turbulent-cfd), then closures with error bounds for canonical flows, then (data-gated) engineering closures (prop-closure-theory, hyper-sbli-heating-closure). Band = judged chance the result is established (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance) by 2031; the engineering implication is judged separately and is Low (P5->P6).

add_nodes.title: Clay recognizes an AI answer to unforced Navier–Stokes
add_nodes.description: The Clay Mathematics Institute states that an AI-produced proof settles the unforced 3D Navier–Stokes problem, either global smoothness (statements A/B) or blowup from smooth data with zero force, or changes its Millennium Problems listing to say so. Clay rules need publication in a qualifying outlet, two years, and general acceptance. Engineering effect: nil.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No unforced claim exists. Clay lists Navier–Stokes as unsolved, and its president called the evaluation of the forced claim 'deliberately unhurried'. OpenAI says it will not claim the prize for the forced result. Petrillo-Glimm (Sep 20, 2026) proposed a target for a programmatic unforced search.
add_nodes.why: Chain: an unforced answer passes outside checks (frontier-ns-unforced: S1 2030, S2 2029, S3 2028), then refereed publication (about a year), then the two-year rule and general acceptance, then Clay's advisory board and a special committee (at least 6-12 months). That puts the earliest statement about four years after the check: 2032 in S3, 2033 in S2, 2034 in S1. The only precedent took about seven years from preprint to award (Perelman: 2002-03 to Mar 2010). The institutional clock runs at 1.0x in every scenario; only the start date differs. If Clay first accepts the forced result under (C) or (D), the prize problem is closed and a statement on the unforced case becomes discretionary, so frontier-ns-clay-cd-ruling can pre-empt this node as well as speed it. Bands by 2035: Medium in S3 and S4, where about three years remain after eligibility; Low in S2, where the clock runs out only about 2033; Speculative in S1. Clay may still wait, or never rule without a claimant. This is the event readers will hear as 'AI solved a Millennium problem'. It changes no engine, heat shield or orbit (tl-position-2), and robots add nothing.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Clay may never rule if no one claims the prize, and general acceptance of a long AI-produced proof can take many years. If Clay accepts the forced result first, the prize problem is closed. Even a ruling changes no CFD code, since codes already regularize.
add_nodes.signpost: Refereed publication of an unforced Navier–Stokes proof (either answer) starts the two-year clock; then a Clay statement or a change to its Millennium Problems listing.
add_nodes.note_2035: New for the 2035 horizon: the Clay clock runs out about four years after the outside check, so the earliest year is 2032-34. A Clay ruling on the forced claim can close the prize first. The clock is institutional, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-math-frontier (2026-10-07): new node. Extends the famous-problem chain past frontier-ns-unforced; frontier-ns-clay-cd-ruling keeps the forced claim. | R-math-frontier (2026-10-07): [skeptic] years S3 2031 -> 2032, S2 2032 -> 2033, S1 2033 -> 2034: Clay's board and committee add at least 6-12 months after eligibility, and the only precedent took about seven years; band_2031 Speculative in all scenarios; band_2035 S2 Medium -> Low, S1 Low -> Speculative; pre-emption by the forced ruling added.

add_nodes.title: Certified math on demand reaches the supplier base
add_nodes.description: Tier-2 and tier-3 space suppliers (structures, propulsion components, avionics boxes, thermal hardware) routinely produce analysis with AI-derived proofs, guaranteed error bars or certified rare-event bounds and deliver it in data packages to primes and operators. This is the second wave after the leading firms (frontier-math-unbinds).
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Suppliers run commercial FEA and CFD tools with small specialist teams (general). Research-grade math models are internal to the labs. Export-control (ITAR/EAR) and defense cybersecurity rules limit which models may see supplier technical data (general).
add_nodes.why: Diffusion lags the leaders. Suppliers have small analysis teams, older toolchains, fixed-price contracts and export-control limits on which models may see their data. They adopt after primes and operators (frontier-math-unbinds: S2 2029, S3 2028) and after accredited models run on controlled networks (capability-controlled-data-access: 2028 in S2 and S3). A three-year lag gives S2 2032. S3 is 2031 because near-free cognition from about 2029 makes the service cheap for small firms. Plateau reaches the leaders' step only about 2033, so suppliers fall after 2035. Suppliers run commercial FE and CFD codes, so certified bounds also reach them as tool updates (struct-verified-fe-solvers: S2 2029; prop-cfd-auto-vv: S2 2028; both soft), after the usual version lag and tool validation. Primes speed adoption when they ask for certified bounds in supplier deliverables, which needs a shared rulebook (physclock-credibility-evidence-standard, soft); open-weight models at research level (soft) let small firms run them on their own networks. Bands by 2035: S3 and S4 are High because near-free cognition and certified commercial tools have had about four years to spread, and the node needs no certifier acceptance. S2 is Medium: three years after 2032 is short for many small firms, many build to print, and no contract data requirement is in motion. Effect (judgment): the same 8-14% of engineering hours as at the leaders, plus fewer late design changes from interface rework. Robots do no analysis, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Many suppliers build to print, and the prime owns most analysis, so supplier math was never the bottleneck. Small firms adopt what customers demand, and liability keeps human sign-off.
add_nodes.signpost: A prime, NASA or Space Force contract data requirement asks suppliers for analysis with certified error bounds or machine-checked derivations; or an industry or agency survey finds most surveyed space suppliers delivering AI-produced analysis.
add_nodes.note_2035: New for the 2035 horizon: the second wave after the leading firms lands about 2032 in the base case. Robots do no analysis, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-math-frontier (2026-10-07): new node. Extends frontier-math-unbinds to the supply chain in 2032-35. | R-math-frontier (2026-10-07): [advocate, partly] commercial-solver channel added, with soft edges from struct-verified-fe-solvers and prop-cfd-auto-vv; S2 High and S1 Low rejected (three years is short for many small firms; S1 lands after 2035). [skeptic, rejected] S3 High kept: the node needs no certifier acceptance, so the regulatory cap does not apply, and certified bounds arrive inside the commercial tools suppliers already run.

add_nodes.title: A certifier audits AI analysis instead of redoing it
add_nodes.description: A certifying authority or mission-assurance office accepts AI-produced analysis with guaranteed bounds from verified numerics and independently checked derivations as certification evidence. Its specialists audit a sample of the key stress, thermal and GNC analyses instead of re-running all of them, so specialist re-analysis stops setting the pace of certification. The likely first case is uncrewed: NASA Launch Services certification of a launch vehicle for high-priority payloads (NPD 8610.7) or Space Force mission assurance for national security launches. A crewed delta certification comes later.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: NASA-STD-7009B (Mar 2024) requires a credibility assessment for models and simulations and has no route for AI-produced analysis. DO-333 covers formal methods in airborne software only (general). NASA launch-vehicle certification (NPD 8610.7) and Space Force mission assurance, where the Aerospace Corporation re-runs analyses, rely on independent specialist re-analysis (general). The NASA Engineering and Safety Center was set up after Columbia to give independent assessments (general). No authority has accepted AI-produced analysis as certification evidence.
add_nodes.why: The design-side outcome (frontier-math-unbinds) runs under each program's own sign-off. Certification is where scarce specialists still set the schedule, because certifiers re-run key analyses themselves. Dropping that step needs a rulebook for AI-made analysis (physclock-credibility-evidence-standard: S2 2029, S3 2028) and guaranteed bounds from verified numerics (infra-verified-numerics: S2 and S3 2028). Certifiers will likely re-run in full the first analyses that earn test credit (physclock-qual-by-analysis-credit: S2 2031, S3 2030, soft). The audit step then needs one delta certification, about 2-3 years. A full human-rating cycle takes about 6 years (Crew Dragon: 2014 to 2020), so the first case is uncrewed. Hence S2 2033 and S3 2032. Plateau gets the rulebook late, so the node falls after 2035. A software-proof precedent helps (infra-tool-qualification, soft), and so does crewed AI-proof credit (verif-hls-autonomy-certification, soft). Credit for Lean-checked derivations of analysis needs a qualified proof kernel, which no node models yet. Certifiers that re-run analyses with their own AI (physclock-regulator-ai-capacity, soft) shorten re-analysis earlier; this node marks the later step of dropping it. This node replaces specialist re-analysis. struct-35-test-standards-codify-ai-credit replaces tests, and verif-35-standards-proof-route covers software proofs. Bands: certifier acceptance with no named mechanism in motion caps 2035 at Medium (S3, S4). S2 is Low because only about two years remain after its earliest date. Institutional clocks set the date, so robots give no S4 credit. Effect: shorter review cycles for certified vehicles; tests and flights do not shorten (tl-position-4).
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Certifiers answer for crew safety and may keep human re-derivation of critical analyses whatever the tools. Review time is mostly test evidence, boards and paperwork, so removing math checks saves little calendar time.
add_nodes.signpost: NASA Launch Services, Space Force mission assurance, the FAA or ESA accepts a certification package in which AI-produced analysis with guaranteed bounds replaces independent specialist re-analysis, with humans auditing a sample. A crewed delta certification that does the same is the second signpost.
add_nodes.note_2035: New for the 2035 horizon: certifiers move from re-running AI analysis to auditing it about two years after analysis first earns test credit, so 2032-33 in S2-S4, first on uncrewed vehicles. Institutional clocks bind, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-math-frontier (2026-10-07): new node. Dates the certification step that frontier-math-unbinds leaves out. | R-math-frontier (2026-10-07): [skeptic] retitled; rescoped to uncrewed certification first, with crewed delta certification as the second signpost; hard edge from infra-tool-qualification made soft (it covers software plans, and analysis evidence runs through NASA-STD-7009); hard edge from infra-verified-numerics added (no year moves); lag restated as one delta certification of 2-3 years against about 6 for human rating; soft edges from verif-hls-autonomy-certification and to struct-35-crewed-structure-analysis-credit. [advocate, partly] soft edge from physclock-qual-by-analysis-credit added; the one-year pull and S2 Medium rejected, because certifiers will re-run the first credited analyses, so the audit step follows those credits.

add_nodes.title: AI settles a Millennium problem other than Navier–Stokes
add_nodes.description: An AI-produced proof settles the Riemann hypothesis, the Yang–Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture or the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, either way, and passes outside checks (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance). Navier–Stokes and P vs NP have their own nodes. Engineering effect: nil.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Open. Fortune (Oct 7, 2026) reported progress by OpenAI, short of solutions, on three other Millennium problems; no manuscript is public, so the report is T1 at best. The Riemann hypothesis is already stated in Lean's Mathlib, so a Lean proof could be checked quickly; the other three need library work before they can be stated in Lean (general).
add_nodes.premise_tier: T1 at best (press report of progress, no manuscript)
add_nodes.why: A scenario signpost with no hardware effect. Unforced Navier–Stokes has a forced precursor; these four problems have none, and Yang–Mills and Hodge also need posing and library work before a check. Judgment: several doublings beyond the unforced Navier–Stokes rung. S3 reaches near-free cognition about 2029, so a checked result is credible from 2030 and about as likely as not by 2035 (Medium). S2 gets cheap and abundant cognition only in 2033-35, so 2033 at the earliest and Low by 2035. S1 falls after 2035. Either answer counts. Reported progress is T1 at best, so no band goes above Medium. A move from Erdos-tier to Millennium-tier results outside fluids is the clearest public test of S3 against S2 in 2032-35. Robots add nothing, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Even a proof of the Riemann hypothesis changes no engine, orbit or flight code. The problems may need ideas that scaling does not supply, as for P vs NP.
add_nodes.signpost: A lab claims one of the four problems with a Lean proof or a full manuscript, followed by a Comparator pass and statement audit, or by acceptance from specialists in the field.
add_nodes.note_2035: New for the 2035 horizon. A scenario signpost: Recursive cognition makes a Millennium result outside fluids about as likely as not by 2035, and the base case is Low. Robots add nothing, so S4 equals S3.
add_nodes.revision_note: R-math-frontier (2026-10-07): new node from the advocate review, added to branch members only. The proposed soft edge from frontier-ns-unforced was dropped, because fluid methods do not carry to these problems.

patch.thesis: If AI settles famous fluid problems, the theorems change almost no engine, heat shield or orbit. Engineers get proof machinery and on-demand error bars from about 2028 (base case). Math stops limiting leading programs about 2029 and suppliers about 2032. Certifiers start auditing AI analysis instead of redoing it about 2033. Robots (S4) speed nothing here. The one link runs the other way: reachability math feeds robot safety envelopes.
patch.band_note: For tier-1 math nodes, band_2031 is the judged chance the result is established (T4 Lean check or T2+ expert acceptance) by 2031; the engineering implication is judged separately in why (usually nil to Low, via P5). For tier-2 applied nodes it is the chance the capability is available and used as the signpost describes. Bands are judgments, not computed probabilities. band_2035 has the same meaning at end-2035.
